and Your Record", "learner_facing": true, "markdown": "## C — Suspensions and Your Record

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A01
Displaying a license known to be canceled, suspended, or changed is unlawful, and changing a driver license is also illegal, with either act able to lead to suspension of driving privileges [A01].
Why it matters: separates fraud behavior from ordinary moving violations.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A01
Utah keeps a computerized driving and crash history for each driver, holding moving-violation convictions and suspensions from the prior three years while alcohol and drug related violations, suspensions, and revocations stay listed for 10 years [A01].
Why it matters: retention windows explain what still counts on the record.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A01
Operating a vehicle while denied, suspended, or revoked can bring a jail term of 90 days plus a fine, and the original denial, suspension, or revocation period grows by an amount equal to that original period [A01].
Why it matters: penalty plus extension is the core deterrent rule.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A01
When the underlying suspension or revocation rests on an alcohol-related offense, the fine can reach up to $1000 with imprisonment for up to six months, and a vehicle driven during a DUI, drug-metabolite, automobile-homicide, alcohol-restricted-driver, or chemical-test-refusal suspension may be impounded [A01].
Why it matters: alcohol-based violations carry the heavier enforcement tier.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A02
A driving privilege faces mandatory suspension, potentially lasting as long as two years or until age 21, for causes including a mandatory-suspension conviction, an injury, fatal, or serious-property-damage crash caused by reckless or unlawful conduct, fraudulent license use, enough convictions to trigger the point system, DUI arrest or drug-offense guilt, and failure to appear or satisfy court fees, fines, or restitution [A02].
Why it matters: groups the conduct and compliance failures that suspend rather than revoke.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A02
That same suspension authority also covers missing no-fault insurance or financial responsibility, operating or permitting operation without required coverage, unpaid child support, a court-ordered texting-violation suspension, under-21 misuse of false age proof for alcohol or bar entry, custodial interference, missing the required four-hour live safety course after an emergency-vehicle approach violation, and a one-year court-ordered suspension on a first road-rage-enhanced citation [A02].
Why it matters: shows non-driving compliance items can suspend the privilege.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A02
Revocation is mandatory upon court guilt for manslaughter or automobile homicide while driving, a repeat intoxicated or measurable-substance driving offense including prescribed medication cases, false sworn license-application statements, felony use of a vehicle including automobile homicide, and failure to stop and aid after a crash causing death or injury [A02].
Why it matters: revocation marks the most serious criminal-driving category.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A03
Further revocation grounds include two reckless or impaired driving charges within one year, fleeing or refusing to stop for a police visual or audible signal, firing or permitting firearm discharge from a vehicle, using or causing explosive, chemical, or incendiary material from a vehicle, driving with detectable alcohol under alcohol-restricted status, and driving without a required ignition interlock device [A03].
Why it matters: completes the willful-danger and restriction-violation set.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A03
Utah assigns 80 points for reckless driving, 35-75 points for speeding based on severity, 60 points each for failure to yield, close following, wrong side of road, and wrong way on a one-way street, 50 points each for red-light, stop-sign, improper-lookout, improper-passing, and texting-while-driving violations, and 40 points for other moving violations [A03].
Why it matters: exact point table drives every threshold calculation.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A03
A driver over 21 who gathers 200 or more points inside a three-year span is called to a hearing, while a driver under 21 is called at 70 or more points inside a three-year span [A03].
Why it matters: age-specific trigger is highly testable.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A03
After the hearing the driver may receive probation, be asked to complete the defensive driving course, or face denial or suspension of the privilege for one month to one year according to the driving history [A03].
Why it matters: outcome range turns the hearing into a consequence.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A04
Driving a full year with no moving-violation conviction removes half of the points on the record, while driving two successive clean years removes all points [A04].
Why it matters: rewards sustained violation-free driving in steps.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A04
Points tied to a single conviction leave the record automatically three years after the violation date [A04].
Why it matters: per-conviction expiry differs from bulk clean-driving removal.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A04
Finishing a division-recommended defensive driving course can delete 50 points, allowed only once within any three-year period, and that point-reduction course is distinct from traffic school sometimes offered through courts [A04].
Why it matters: one-time reduction versus court school is a classic confusable.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0083]

High-yield ranked: 1) point values and hearing thresholds; 2) point clearance and defensive-course reduction; 3) driving-while-suspended penalties and extension; 4) suspension versus revocation triggers; 5) record retention and license-fraud rules.
Misconceptions: suspension and revocation are interchangeable; any clean year erases all points; court traffic school and the 50-point defensive course are the same; under-21 and adult point limits match.
Mnemonics: 200-70-3 for hearing limits by age over three years; half-then-all for one clean year versus two clean years.
Glossary: suspension is a temporary loss of driving privilege; revocation is termination of driving privilege by court action; denial is refusal of driving privilege; MVR is the computerized driving and crash record; point system is Utah Driver Improvement Program scoring of violations.
Dynamic-fact isolation: office locations, fees, and current course-provider details are updatable and not stated as stable facts in this chunk.
